title_ar: الاعتبار بمرور الزمن .. و حرمة العلماء
title_en: Taking Heed from the Passing of Time, and the Inviolability of the Scholars
body_ar: تحدث فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو الشنقيطي ـ حفظه الله تعالى في خطبة الجمعة " 31-10-2014"الموافق "7-1-1436"عن السنة الهجرية الجديدة و فضل شهر الله المحرّم داعيا إلى أخذ العبرة من مرور الزمن و تعاقب الأيام و أذن ذلك يقرب الانسان إلى الدار الآخرة وهو ما يتطلب الاستعداد و المسارعة إلى الخيرات ، كما تحدث فضيلته عن فضل العلماء و مكانتهم بصفتهم ورثة الأنبياء و الموقعين عن الله داعيا في هذا السياق إلى توقير العلماء و توفير الحرمة لهم، واستنكر الشيخ الاعتداء على العلماء مبينا أنه منكر شنيع لا سيما إذا كان في بيوت الله فإن ذلك مما تتضاعف به الحرمة و تعظم به الهيبة.. وقد قال تعالى: " ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله فهو خير له عند ربه " .
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew al-Shinqiti (may God the Exalted preserve him) spoke in the Friday sermon of '31-10-2014', corresponding to '7-1-1436', about the new Hijri year and the merit of the month of God, Muharram, calling for a lesson to be drawn from the passing of time and the succession of days, and for the recognition that this brings a person nearer to the abode of the hereafter — which calls for preparation and for hastening towards good works.

His Eminence also spoke of the merit of the scholars and their standing, in that they are the heirs of the prophets and those who sign on God's behalf, calling in this connection for the scholars to be honoured and for their inviolability to be upheld.

The Sheikh condemned assaults upon scholars, explaining that this is a hideous wrong, and the more so if it takes place in the houses of God, for that is among the things by which the inviolability is doubled and the awe made greater. God the Exalted has said: {That — and whoever magnifies the sanctities of God, it is better for him with his Lord} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:30).

flags.context: بصفتهم ورثة الأنبياء و الموقعين عن الله
options: those who sign on God's behalf
those who issue rulings in God's name
flags.note: The phrase is Ibn al-Qayyim's, from the title of Iʿlām al-Muwaqqiʿīn ʿan Rabb al-ʿĀlamīn, and figures the jurist as one who signs a document on behalf of the sovereign. The image must survive: rendering it 'those who issue rulings' loses the whole force of the expression, which is what makes the following call for their inviolability more than a courtesy. Not in the project glossary.

The English keeps it general because the Arabic is general. A reviewer or the Sheikh's office may be able to supply the occasion, which would change how the passage should be displayed.

flags.context: داعيا إلى أخذ العبرة من مرور الزمن و تعاقب الأيام و أذن ذلك يقرب الانسان إلى الدار الآخرة

translator_notes: A news report of a Friday sermon, not the sermon's text; typed 'news' for that reason.

حرمة is rendered 'inviolability' rather than 'sanctity' where it is used of the scholars, and 'sanctities' in the Qur'anic quotation (حرمات الله), which is the standard English there. The record plays on the two senses.

The source encloses the Qur'anic text in ordinary quotation marks and gives no reference; the English identifies it as Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:30 and uses the corpus convention. Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
